full_judgment:
2. The property in question is the house No. 19/7 Block E Azam Road PS Mohammadpur, Dhaka. This property was enlisted in the 'Ka' list of the abandoned properties on 23-9-1986. Claiming title and possession in this property, the writ petitioner Wahidul Haque filed .a case bearing No. 64/92 in the 1st Court of Settlement Dhaka praying for release of the property from the list of abandoned property. The Settlement Court by its judgment and order dated 15-11-1994, dismissed that case. The petitioner then filed writ petition No. 2328 of 1994 against that judgment and order of the Settlement Court and obtained Rule which was ultimately made absolute on 14-3-1999. In the judgment of that writ petition it was clearly held by their Lordships that the enlistment of the property in question as abandoned property was illegal. Their Lordships, however, further observed that the title of the writ petitioner in the property in question would be decided in Title Suit No. 277 of 1991 of the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka which was then being contested by the respondents. That Title Suit No. 277 of 1991 also was ultimately decreed on contest on 12-8-1999 declaring petitioner's title in the suit land and also declaring that the suit land was not vested and non-resident property. The respondents did not prefer any appeal against any of the above judgments of the courts till date. Thus having two judgments in his favour from competent courts of law the petitioner applied to the Ministry of Housing and Public Works for formal release of the property in question and also for mutating his name in records of the property in question. But the petitioner did not get any positive response from the respondents, rather was informed by some of the respondents that until and unless the Ministry of Housing and Public Works issued a fresh release order and published that in the official Gazette, the respondents would not mutate the name of the petitioner in respect of the property in question. The petitioner approached the respondents several times and requested them to implement the judgments of the courts of law by mutating his name in the records of the property in question but did not get any result. The respondents have given direction to other authorities also like WASA, DESA, City Corporation etc. not to treat the petitioner as owner of the property in question until and unless a fresh release order is issued from the Ministry of Housing and Public Works in respect of the property in question. The petitioner thus having faced much inconvenience in the enjoyment of his property has been compelled to come to this court against this fresh writ petition and obtained the Rule. 

 9. However, in the present case, obviously, the respondents, by not giving effect to the judgments within a long period of more than two years on the plea that the concerned Ministry has not yet made a release order by gazette notification, have willfully flouted the court's order which justify initiation of a contempt proceeding. It is clearly stated here again that after the decision of the courts of law declaring any property as not being abandoned property a further release order of the same property by the government is not necessary at all, because from the date of such judgment the property stands excluded from the list of abandoned properties. If the government, for its convenience or other reasons wants to make a gazette notification that the property has been excluded from the abandoned properties list, as per judgment and decree of the court of law it may do so, but for that reason it cannot refuse or defer the decree holder's prayer for mutation of his name and acceptance of rent from him or his other acts in enjoyment of that property.
